classification.difficultyReason: Account for exposed surfaces across joined and hollow solids, excluding both contact faces and including tunnel walls. The hardest part links Pythagoras for a triangular prism's slope with subtraction of its rectangular contact area from the combined surface areas.

content.prompt: Find the surface area of these composite solids. Round to 1 d.p. where appropriate.

spec.description: Two coaxial cylinders with diameter arrows, exposed annular shoulder and dashed hidden lower arcs.
spec.mathematics: Upper radius 2 cm, height 4 cm; lower radius 3 cm, height 2 cm.

answer.worked:
The joined circles are internal surfaces.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{bottom}}&=\pi(3)^2=9\pi\\
A_{\text{lower curved surface}}&=2\pi(3)(2)=12\pi\\
A_{\text{annulus}}&=\pi(3)^2-\pi(2)^2=5\pi\\
A_{\text{upper curved surface}}&=2\pi(2)(4)=16\pi\\
A_{\text{top}}&=\pi(2)^2=4\pi\\
\text{SA}&=9\pi+12\pi+5\pi+16\pi+4\pi\\
\text{SA}&=46\pi\approx144.5\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Cube on a rectangular prism, with three single equality ticks on the cube and external dimension labels.
spec.mathematics: Base 20 by 12 by 8 cm; upper cube side 3 cm.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{base prism}}&=2(20\times12+20\times8+12\times8)\\
A_{\text{base prism}}&=992\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{cube}}&=6(3^2)=54\text{ cm}^2\\
\text{SA}&=992+54-2(3^2)\\
\text{SA}&=1028\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
Subtract both joined square faces.

spec.description: Cylinder on a cube, with cube double ticks and dashed hidden edges. No cylinder diameter label is added.
spec.mathematics: Cube side 10 m; cylinder height 8 m; cylinder radius is not explicitly given.

answer.worked:
Taking the cylinder diameter as $10\text{ m}$ gives $r=5\text{ m}$. The removed circle on the cube and the exposed top circle have equal areas.
$$\begin{align*}
\text{SA}&=6(10^2)-\pi(5)^2+2\pi(5)(8)+\pi(5)^2\\
\text{SA}&=600+80\pi\\
\text{SA}&\approx851.3\text{ m}^2
\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right-triangular prism on a rectangular base. All six source measurements retained; decorative grey face shading omitted.
spec.mathematics: Base 100 by 100 by 26 cm. Upper triangular cross-section has legs 100 and 65 cm and prism length 40 cm. Front exposed strip is 30 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; calculated hypotenuse and area omitted.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
s&=\sqrt{100^2+65^2}=\sqrt{14225}\text{ cm}\\
A_{\text{base}}&=2(100\times100+100\times26+100\times26)\\
A_{\text{base}}&=30400\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{upper prism}}&=2\left(\tfrac12\times100\times65\right)+40(100+65+\sqrt{14225})\\
\text{SA}&=30400+6500+40(165+\sqrt{14225})-2(100\times40)\\
\text{SA}&=35500+40\sqrt{14225}\\
\text{SA}&\approx40\,270.7\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
Subtract both joined rectangles. The $30\text{ cm}$ strip locates the upper prism and does not change the total exposed area.
